titulo: Adjetivos 1: with the definite article (der große Mann): Nominativo e acusativo

aula.titulo: Adjetivos 1: with the definite article (der große Mann)
aula.objetivo: Give the adjective its ending before the noun, after der, die, das: the two endings -e and -en, in the four cases.

blocos.texto: Goal of the lesson. By the end of the four sessions, you choose the right adjective ending before the noun (ein großer Tisch, der große Tisch, kalter Kaffee), using a three-question method instead of memorising tables.

blocos.contexto: Camila shows her room and a photo of home.

linhas.ru: — Danke! Ich habe einen neuen Tisch und eine kleine Lampe.
linhas.en: — Thanks! I have a new desk and a small lamp.
linhas.audio: Danke! Ich habe einen neuen Tisch und eine kleine Lampe.

linhas.ru: — Und wer ist der junge Mann auf dem Foto?
linhas.en: — And who is the boy in the photo?
linhas.audio: Und wer ist der junge Mann auf dem Foto?

linhas.ru: — Das ist mein jüngerer Bruder Pedro.
linhas.audio: Das ist mein jüngerer Bruder Pedro.

linhas.ru: — Das ist unser altes Haus, mit dem großen Garten und den bunten Blumen.
linhas.en: — That's our old house, with the big garden and the colourful flowers.
linhas.audio: Das ist unser altes Haus, mit dem großen Garten und den bunten Blumen.

linhas.ru: — Wie schön! Du hast eine tolle Familie.
linhas.en: — How lovely! You have a great family.
linhas.audio: Wie schön! Du hast eine tolle Familie.

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: without an article, or without a sign of gender and case, the adjective takes over that job. With a sign, the adjective just rests on -e or -en.
blocos.comparacao: English puts the adjective before the noun and never changes it: “new table, new tables”. German also puts it before the noun, but it changes by gender, number and case, and it depends on which article comes before it.

blocos.titulo: The adjective before the noun, step by step
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: after «sein», the adjective does NOT change: «Der Mann ist groß». STEP 2: BEFORE the noun, it gets an ENDING: «der große Mann». STEP 3: after the definite article (der, die, das), there are only two endings: «-e» and «-en». STEP 4: in the NOMINATIVE singular, it is always «-e»: der große Mann, die kleine Frau, das neue Auto. In the plural, «-en»: die großen Kinder. STEP 5: in the ACCUSATIVE, only the MASCULINE changes: «den großen Mann» (-en); feminine and neuter stay «-e»: «die kleine Frau», «das neue Auto»; the plural stays «-en». STEP 6: the ending repeats the case that the article has already shown: the adjective only «reinforces» it when the article is not enough.
blocos.comparacao: English never changes the adjective («the tall man», «the tall women»). German changes it by gender, number and CASE, but after der/die/das there are only two endings: -e and -en.

erros.motivo: Before the noun, the adjective takes an ending.

blocos.enunciado: Describe 6 people or things with the definite article and an adjective: «Der freundliche Mann … Das neue Auto … Die kleinen Kinder …»
Write out from memory the table of the definite articles in the four cases.
